expectations.text: Covers the GDPR Art. 28(3) mandatory clause set: documented instructions, confidentiality, security measures, sub-processor rules, data subject rights assistance, breach notification, deletion/return at end, audit rights
expectations.evidence: Checklist covers "Documented instructions... Confidentiality... Security (Art. 32 reference)... Sub-processor authorization... Data subject rights assistance... Breach notification... Deletion/return at termination... Audit rights"

expectations.text: Explains sub-processor authorisation mechanics (Art. 28(2)): specific or general written authorisation with change notification and objection opportunity, plus equivalent flow-down (Art. 28(4)) and processor liability
expectations.evidence: Covers Art. 28(2) specific vs general authorisation with objection/notice and Art. 28(4) flow-down, but omits processor liability (initial processor remains fully liable for sub-processor failures)

expectations.text: Reviews the sub-processor list for fourth-party concentration, transfer destinations/mechanisms, and change-notification lead time
expectations.evidence: "fourth-party concentration (are multiple critical functions routed through the same hyperscaler...)"; "transfer destinations and mechanisms... SCCs, adequacy"; "change-notification lead time (30 days is reasonable...)"

expectations.text: States that US employee health data for a benefits program raises HIPAA business associate questions: a DPA is not a BAA — 45 CFR 164.308(b)/164.314(a) assurances are separate
expectations.evidence: "a GDPR DPA is a distinct legal instrument from a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement"; "satisfactory assurances via a BAA... 45 CFR 164.308(b)(1)"; "(per 164.314(a))"

expectations.text: Produces an actionable clause-by-clause output (present/absent/deficient or checklist form) rather than generic prose
expectations.evidence: "Go clause-by-clause and mark each present/absent/deficient" with an explicit clause checklist
